issues.legal_issue: A statutory proceeding to frame a scheme for the management of a temple is an exhaustive inquiry rather than a summary proceeding.
material_facts: The Board framed a scheme for the temple under the statutory provision governing temple schemes.
The statutory scheme made the Board’s order final subject to a suit to modify or set it aside, and the court proceeding was to be tried in the manner of an ordinary civil suit.
issues.conclusion: The Board’s power to frame a scheme was not summary; the statutory process provided for an exhaustive inquiry by the Board and, if challenged, by the court.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 57(1) and 57(3) of the Madras Religious and Charitable Endowments Act, 1927, the Board could settle a scheme, and an interested person could bring a suit to modify or set aside its order. The court proceeding was to be tried as an ordinary suit under the Civil Procedure Code. The Court relied on (Sri Mahant) Sitaram Dass Bavaji v. Madras Religious Endowment Board, Madras, and Arikapudi Balakotayya v. Yadlapalli Nagayya.

predicates.temple_scheme_proceeding: An authority considers framing a scheme for the management of a temple.
predicates.board_conducts_inquiry: The authority examines matters relevant to framing the temple-management scheme.
predicates.court_challenge_available: An affected person can challenge the authority’s scheme order in court, where the matter is tried as an ordinary suit.

issues.definition: When a temple-management scheme is considered and the authority examines relevant matters or an ordinary court challenge is available, the proceeding is not summary.

issues.legal_issue: A final determination of property rights in a proceeding to frame a temple-management scheme can operate as res judicata in a later proceeding concerning the same property.
material_facts: During the Board’s 1931 scheme proceeding, the respondent’s family claimed that the disputed properties had been granted as service inam and were not temple properties.
The Board accepted that claim, thereby determining that the properties were not temple properties.
Identifying the temple’s properties was necessary to frame a management scheme, and the determination affected the temple’s rights substantially.
The temple could have challenged the Board’s decision by filing a suit under Section 57(3), but did not do so; the decision became final.
The later suit concerned the same properties and the competing claims to them.
issues.conclusion: The Board’s unchallenged decision that the disputed properties were not temple properties operated as res judicata in the later proceeding, so the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Res judicata is not confined to decisions in suits or to the limits of Section 11 of the Civil Procedure Code; it may apply to other proceedings where the decision determines substantial rights and the parties have an adequate opportunity to establish their claims. Its underlying purposes include finality in litigation and preventing a person from being vexed twice over the same matter. A temple scheme must identify the institution’s assets. The Court relied on Chotalal Lakhmiram v. Manohar Ganesh Tambekar, (Sri Mahant) Sitaram Dass Bavaji v. Madras Religious Endowment Board, Madras, Arikapudi Balakotayya v. Yadlapalli Nagayya, and State of Madras v. Kunnakudi Melamatam alias Annathana Matam, as well as Sections 57(1) and 57(3) of the Madras Religious and Charitable Endowments Act, 1927.

rule.if: later_proceeding_concerns_same_property and prior_scheme_proceeding and property_rights_determined and property_identification_needed_for_scheme and determination_substantially_affected_rights and adequate_opportunity_to_establish_rights and challenge_not_pursued and prior_determination_final

predicates.later_proceeding_concerns_same_property: A later proceeding concerns property whose ownership was determined in an earlier proceeding.
predicates.prior_scheme_proceeding: An authority previously considered a scheme for the management of a temple.
predicates.property_rights_determined: The authority decided whether the disputed property belonged to the institution or to another claimant.
predicates.property_identification_needed_for_schem: Identifying the institution’s property was necessary to frame its management scheme.
predicates.determination_substantially_affected_rig: The authority’s decision materially affected a party’s rights in the disputed property.
predicates.adequate_opportunity_to_establish_rights: The parties had an adequate opportunity to establish their claimed rights in the earlier proceeding and its available court challenge.
predicates.challenge_not_pursued: The party against whom the determination was made did not pursue the available challenge to it.
predicates.prior_determination_final: The earlier property determination became final.

issues.definition: If a final property determination made in a temple-scheme proceeding substantially affected rights, the parties had an adequate opportunity to establish those rights, no available challenge was pursued, and a later proceeding concerns the same property, the prior determination operates as res judicata.
